added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(\beta>0\) and \(D\in(0,1/4]\). Put
\[
A_{n,m,\tau}:=\ell\min\{1,N^{-\varkappa}\},
\qquad L_m:=\log(2m).
\]
There are constants \(0<c_{\beta,D}\le C_{\beta,D}<\infty\), depending only on \(\beta,D\), such that for every \(n\ge2\), every even \(m\ge2\), and every \(0<\tau\le1/(8n)\) satisfying
\[
A_{n,m,\tau}<L_m^{1-\varkappa},
\qquad
A_{n,m,\tau}\left(1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}\right)\ge\ell,
\]
one has
\[
c_{\beta,D}\ell
\le \mathcal R(n,m,\tau)
\le C_{\beta,D}\ell.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\frac12\ell\le \mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)\le\ell,
\]
so \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\asymp_{\beta,D}\ell\asymp\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)\) throughout this saturated sub-familywise phase. Every case with \(N<1\) that satisfies the first, sub-familywise, inequality automatically satisfies the second inequality and hence lies in this phase.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Because \(\beta>0\), the definition \(\varkappa=\beta/(2\beta+4)\) gives
\[
0<\varkappa<\frac12,
\qquad
p:=\frac{\varkappa}{1-\varkappa}>0.
\]
Admissibility gives \(\tau<1\), hence \(\ell=\log(1/\tau)>0\), and \(m\ge2\) gives \(L_m=\log(2m)>1\). Since the map \(z\mapsto z^p\) is strictly increasing on \((0,\infty)\), the first displayed hypothesis implies
\[
A_{n,m,\tau}^{p}
<\left(L_m^{1-\varkappa}\right)^p
=L_m^{\varkappa}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\min\left\{A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)},L_m^{\varkappa}\right\}
=A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}.
\]
Applying \(\mathrm{prop{:}multiscale\text{-}paired\text{-}splice\text{-}lower\text{-}envelope}\) and then the second displayed hypothesis therefore yields, equation by equation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)
&\ge c_{\beta,D}\min\!\left\{\ell,
A_{n,m,\tau}\left[1+
\min\!\left\{A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)},L_m^{\varkappa}\right\}\right]\right\}\\
&=c_{\beta,D}\min\!\left\{\ell,
A_{n,m,\tau}\left[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}\right]\right\}\\
&=c_{\beta,D}\ell.
\end{aligned}
\]
On the other hand, \(\mathrm{thm{:}generic\text{-}regret\text{-}sandwich}\) gives
\[
\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)
\le C_{\beta,D}\ell
\min\left\{1,\left(\frac{mL_m}{n}\right)^{\varkappa}\right\}
=C_{\beta,D}\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)
\le C_{\beta,D}\ell,
\]
where the middle equality is the construction in \(\mathrm{def{:}coordinatewise\text{-}hall\text{-}baseline}\).

For completeness, that construction and \(N=n/m\) imply the useful identity
\[
\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)
=\min\{\ell,A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa}\}.
\]
Indeed, if \(N\ge1\), then \(A_{n,m,\tau}=\ell N^{-\varkappa}\), whereas if \(N<1\), both sides equal \(\ell\) because \(L_m>1\). The two regime hypotheses further give
\[
\ell
\le A_{n,m,\tau}\left(1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{p}\right)
<A_{n,m,\tau}(1+L_m^{\varkappa})
\le2A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa},
\]
where the last inequality uses \(L_m^{\varkappa}>1\). Hence
\[
\frac12\ell
\le\min\{\ell,A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa}\}
=\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)
\le\ell.
\]
This proves both comparisons.

Finally, if \(N<1\), then \(N^{-\varkappa}>1\), and therefore
\[
A_{n,m,\tau}=\ell,
\qquad
A_{n,m,\tau}(1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{p})
=\ell(1+\ell^p)\ge\ell.
\]
Thus the saturation inequality is automatic whenever \(N<1\), as claimed.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Put \(A_{n,m,\tau}:=\ell\min\{1,N^{-\varkappa}\}\) and \(L_m:=\log(2m)\). Restrict the unresolved regret problem to the unsaturated strict sub-familywise region
\[
A_{n,m,\tau}<L_m^{1-\varkappa},
\qquad
A_{n,m,\tau}\left[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}\right]<\ell.
\]
No case with \(N<1\) lies in this region. The proved bounds there are
\[
c_{\beta,D}A_{n,m,\tau}
\left[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}\right]
\le\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)
\le C_{\beta,D}\min\{\ell,A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa}\}
=C_{\beta,D}\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau).
\]
Determine \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\) up to constants depending only on \(\beta,D\) within this remaining region. In particular, construct one computable capacity-aware learner over the full heterogeneous class \(\mathcal H_{\beta,D}(m)\) that attains the lower expression, including sparse-dominance, collective-contribution, and local-to-tied mixtures, or prove that another same-class configuration raises the lower bound. Determine whether \(A_{n,m,\tau}\to0\), which is necessary for vanishing regret, is sufficient, or whether the stronger currently sufficient condition \(A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa}\to0\) is necessary. Equivalently, identify the maximal subregimes of this unsaturated phase on which capacity averaging yields \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)=o\{\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)\}\). The existing coordinatewise learner \(\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{tail}}\) remains only the upper witness; no nonzero policy-selection price is assumed.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current question still includes a saturated strict sub-familywise subset. The accepted multiscale lower envelope and generic upper bound now prove regret of order \(\ell\) on that subset, so only the complementary unsaturated subset is genuinely unresolved. This narrows a regime quantifier and does not assume the missing selected-mixture oracle inequality.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Tensorize two-arm Hall splices across paired cells at an arbitrary admissible amplitude, retain the exact logarithmic mixture loss, condition on the pair sample counts, factor the product posterior, and compare every feasible zero-, one-, or two-cell capacity allocation with one posterior-MAP action per pair by concavity. A binomial lower-tail calculation followed by amplitude optimization gives the multiscale same-class lower envelope. Put \(A_{n,m,\tau}:=\ell\min\{1,N^{-\varkappa}\}\) and \(L_m:=\log(2m)\). Comparing that envelope with the separate coordinatewise sorting-and-inversion upper witness closes the familywise phase \(A_{n,m,\tau}\ge L_m^{1-\varkappa}\), including saturation. In the strict sub-familywise phase, the envelope and the generic upper bound also give \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\asymp_{\beta,D}\ell\asymp\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)\) whenever \(A_{n,m,\tau}[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}]\ge\ell\); this includes every \(N<1\) case satisfying the sub-familywise inequality. The only unresolved region is therefore
\[
A_{n,m,\tau}<L_m^{1-\varkappa},
\qquad
A_{n,m,\tau}\left[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}\right]<\ell.
\]
There the construction supplies the lower rate \(A_{n,m,\tau}[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}]\), while the known coordinatewise upper witness supplies \(\min\{\ell,A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa}\}\); no localized selected-mixture upper witness or harder same-class lower configuration is built into this handle.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The current handle incorrectly describes the whole strict sub-familywise phase as unresolved. The lower envelope saturates at \(\ell\) when \(A_{n,m,\tau}[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}]\ge\ell\), and the generic upper bound is then matching; the construction must isolate only the remaining unsaturated region.

proposed.justification: The familywise phase, the saturated strict sub-familywise phase, and the all-vanishing-regime regular-policy comparison are settled; the remaining headline contribution is exactly the localized selected-mixture frontier in the unsaturated strict sub-familywise region.
proposed.gap: CarpentierKim2015 supplies translated one-tail familywise machinery but no randomized capacity-selected mixture oracle inequality in the remaining unsaturated region, and AtheyWager2021 supplies no moving extreme-mixture rate.
proposed.consumer: Resolving the remaining unsaturated gap would tell users of the non-nested upper-cost-quantile objective in OsamaZachariahStoica2020 exactly when capacity averaging permits reliable Hall extrapolation beyond both certified obstruction regions.

obligation.what_is_open: Within \(A_{n,m,\tau}<L_m^{1-\varkappa}\) and \(A_{n,m,\tau}[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}]<\ell\), match the proved lower rate with one computable learner over the full heterogeneous Hall class, or exhibit a harder same-class configuration; thereby decide the exact vanishing criterion and the maximal strict-improvement regimes relative to \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)\).
obligation.obstruction: Simultaneous coordinatewise control attains only \(\min\{\ell,A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa}\}\). In the remaining unsaturated region, the missing oracle inequality must instead control the random mixture mass of severely underestimated arms selected under capacity, uniformly over heterogeneous indices and local ties; the frozen primitives provide no such localized selected-mixture concentration result.
obligation.attempted: The paired product-prior converse, fixed-sample posterior factorization, capacity exchange, binomial missed-cell lower bound, and amplitude optimization close the lower side. Direct algebra from that lower envelope also closes the newly separated saturated sub-familywise region. A natural-threshold empirical minimizer and an average multiplicative core comparison were tried in the remaining region, but rare severe underestimation can be selected adaptively; restoring simultaneous control reproduces the coordinatewise logarithmic factor.

proposed.comparator_claim: The paper estimates a policy maximizing a fixed marginal potential-outcome quantile and derives nonstandard fixed-level asymptotics.

Its one-tail Hall results motivate the coordinatewise benchmark after the translation \(\beta_{\mathrm{CK}}=\beta/\alpha\). Each conditional tail here is a compact translated slice of that one-tail class, while the full randomized \(2m\)-tail causal experiment is a stricter product construction. The translated coordinatewise benchmark is minimax-equivalent in the familywise phase and the saturated strict sub-familywise phase, but the unsaturated capacity-mixture upper frontier does not follow from their theorems.

Theorem 1 lower-bounds honest scalar tail confidence length by worst-case bias and the paper constructs a bias-aware interval.
Theorems 4.3 and 5.1 give process inference for extreme treatment contrasts over tail levels and fixed treatment pairs.
The manuscript derives finite-sample minimax-regret treatment rules for a fixed quantile with outcomes restricted to the unit interval.

prose_updates.tldr: Capacity-constrained treatment choice at a beyond-sample loss quantile is governed by the inverse of a selected heterogeneous survival mixture. The coordinatewise benchmark is minimax-sharp throughout the familywise phase \(A_{n,m,\tau}\ge[\log(2m)]^{1-\varkappa}\), including saturation. It is also sharp, at order \(\ell\), in the strict sub-familywise region where \(A_{n,m,\tau}[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}]\ge\ell\); every \(N<1\) case satisfying the sub-familywise inequality lies there. Only the unsaturated strict sub-familywise region retains a selected-mixture regret gap. The simultaneous-inference width converse and exact shrinking criterion remain a separate open question.

project_justification.gap: Published fixed-level quantile-policy methods do not address extrapolated Hall tails. One-tail Hall theory supplies the translated coordinatewise benchmark, which is proved unavoidable both in the familywise phase and on the saturated strict sub-familywise subset, but neither it nor regular policy-learning theory supplies the capacity-aware oracle inequality needed in the remaining unsaturated region.
project_justification.niche: For each fixed even cell count, randomization identifies every policy mixture and capacity optimization is computable by sorting. Heterogeneous indices, local ties, empty observed cells, and growing mixture mass remain in the model; the paired-splice argument handles unrestricted reallocation and, together with the new saturation corollary, isolates the unsaturated strict sub-familywise region where selected-mixture averaging could improve on familywise estimation.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the generic full-class regret sandwich, the exact two-cell frontier, a multiscale paired-splice lower envelope, and the matched coordinatewise frontier in two regions: the familywise phase and the saturated strict sub-familywise phase. It proves that every \(N<1\) sub-familywise case belongs to the latter and that every vanishing-regret sequence remains asymptotically separated from the regular additive-policy benchmark. The only remaining regret problem is the exact upper frontier in the unsaturated strict sub-familywise region; confidence-width optimality remains separate.

prose_updates.related_work: CarpentierKim2015 is one-tail statistical substrate, not a capacity-policy theorem. Each conditional tail in this note is a compact translated slice of its one-tail Hall class after the parameter conversion \(\beta_{\mathrm{CK}}=\beta/\alpha\), while the full randomized causal experiment couples \(2m\) such tails through a stricter product construction. The present paired-splice converse and coordinatewise upper bound prove equivalence to the translated coordinatewise benchmark in the familywise phase and, by saturation, on a strict sub-familywise subset; in the remaining unsaturated region, CarpentierKim2015 supplies no selected-mixture oracle inequality. A paired-splice converse transfers upward only to an explicitly defined superclass containing every constructed full-data law; an upper bound must be rechecked on that superclass and does not transfer from the splice. AtheyWager2021 and KitagawaTetenov2018 concern regular additive welfare, and the proved implication \(\mathcal R/\mathcal B_{\mathrm{AW}}\to\infty\) on every vanishing-regret sequence shows that their \(\sqrt{m/n}\)-type scale is not the extreme-tail frontier. WangZhouSongSherwood2018 and XiaZhangKong2026 occupy fixed-level quantile-policy identification or learning. OsamaZachariahStoica2020 supplies the non-nested marginal upper-cost-quantile consumer objective; it is neither a class-inclusion statement nor a rate engine for this Hall experiment. Its support-based conformal limit motivates the extrapolation question but does not establish the answer. Predetermined heterogeneous-tail pooling, scalar tail intervals, and fixed-pair extreme-treatment inference likewise do not resolve selection among capacity-constrained mixtures.
prose_updates.interpretation: The phase map now has two certified regions. At or above the familywise elbow \(A_{n,m,\tau}=[\log(2m)]^{1-\varkappa}\), rare cellwise errors make coordinatewise calibration minimax-unavoidable. Below the elbow, if the multiscale selected-mixture term \(A_{n,m,\tau}[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}]\) reaches \(\ell\), the logarithmic regret saturates and the coordinatewise benchmark is again sharp; this automatically covers every \(N<1\) case that is sub-familywise. Only when both inequalities are strict can capacity averaging possibly improve the coordinatewise rate.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The distributional lower-side obstruction is resolved. Comparison with the coordinatewise upper theorem closes the familywise phase, and direct use of the lower envelope closes the saturated strict sub-familywise phase at \(\mathcal R\asymp_{\beta,D}\ell\asymp\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}\). The residual regret step is confined to \(A_{n,m,\tau}<L_m^{1-\varkappa}\) and \(A_{n,m,\tau}[1+A_{n,m,\tau}^{\varkappa/(1-\varkappa)}]<\ell\): no proved learner controls data-dependent selected tail weights at the lower rate without reverting to the coordinatewise maximum. Thus \(A_{n,m,\tau}\to0\) is proved necessary and \(A_{n,m,\tau}L_m^{\varkappa}\to0\) sufficient for vanishing regret, but equality of these criteria remains open only inside that last region. The confidence-width converse and exact shrinking condition remain separately open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established claims are the fixed-cell Hall model and identification setup, sorting and inversion, Hall-core approximation, the local-dominance map, the generic coordinatewise regret sandwich, the exact two-cell rate, the simultaneous confidence upper system, the multiscale paired-splice lower envelope, the matched familywise regret frontier, and the saturated strict sub-familywise frontier. The lower envelope is not described as the exact frontier in the remaining unsaturated region. The exact unsaturated capacity-aware upper rate and the sharp confidence-width frontier remain open. No common tail index, fixed gap, density, nonempty realized cell sample, nuisance-rate assumption, or selection penalty is imposed. A paired-splice converse may be exported only to a superclass explicitly containing its full-data laws; the corresponding upper bound requires a separate proof.

statement_notes.justification: This corollary removes a previously unresolved subset by observing that the accepted lower envelope has already reached its maximal logarithmic scale there, while the generic upper bound can never exceed that scale.
statement_notes.gap: It does not provide the localized selected-mixture oracle inequality required when the lower envelope is still below \(\ell\).
statement_notes.consumer: It certifies that capacity averaging cannot yield vanishing regret in this saturated sub-familywise region, including every sub-familywise case with fewer than one expected observation per cell.
